name: Skin Booster
summary: Injectable hydrating treatments used to support skin quality and hydration.
leadAnswer: Skin boosters are injectable treatments that deliver hydrating ingredients into the skin. Which product suits your skin, and whether an injectable is the right route for what is bothering you, is decided by a doctor at consultation.

routes.title: Dull, dry or dehydrated-looking skin
routes.body: Hydration and overall skin quality, and fine lines associated with dryness.

routes.title: Sensitised, acne-affected or post-treatment skin
routes.body: Skin that needs support rather than hydration alone. The polynucleotide boosters, Rejuran and Plinest, are often considered here, once any active acne flare has settled.

routes.title: Texture, pores and the under-eye area
routes.body: Uneven texture and enlarged-looking pores, where a collagen-stimulating booster such as Juvelook is one option, and the under-eye area.

variantModule.heading: Which skin booster, and what is in it
variantModule.intro: Skin booster is an umbrella term, and the products under it are not interchangeable. They differ in their active ingredient.

items.title: Rejuran
items.body: Used to support the skin barrier and skin healing, and often considered for sensitive, acne-prone or damaged skin.

items.title: Plinest / Newest
items.body: A polynucleotide range used to support skin regeneration and elasticity, often considered for stressed, ageing or post-treatment skin. Also fish-derived.

items.title: Profhilo
items.body: A high-concentration hyaluronic acid used for deep hydration and skin remodelling, and to support firmness.

items.title: Hydrodeluxe
items.body: A hyaluronic acid hydrogel enriched with calcium hydroxyapatite and amino acids, used to support skin moisture and overall skin quality.

items.title: Juvelook
items.body: A collagen-stimulating booster used for pores, texture and fine lines.

avoidIf.lead: Active infection, an acne flare or inflammation

avoidIf.body: for Rejuran and Plinest, which are fish-derived, or a known hypersensitivity to hyaluronic acid or another ingredient.

avoidIf.lead: A bleeding disorder or blood-thinning medication.
A tendency to keloid or hypertrophic scarring,
Nodules or granulomatous reactions to a previous filler or biostimulator,
avoidIf.body: which is a consideration for collagen-stimulating products such as Juvelook.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and skin assessment
sessionSteps.body: A doctor examines your skin and decides whether a skin booster suits your concern and, if so, which type: hydrating, polynucleotide or collagen-stimulating.

sessionSteps.title: Preparation
sessionSteps.body: The skin is cleansed and a topical anaesthetic is usually applied and left to take effect, which accounts for much of the appointment time.

sessionSteps.title: The injections
sessionSteps.body: The doctor places the product as a series of small injections across the assessed area.

bands.title: Straight afterwards
bands.body: Small raised bumps at each injection point are expected. Redness, mild swelling and pinpoint bruising can also occur.

bands.title: The first day or two
bands.body: The bumps settle as the product disperses: within hours to about a day for hyaluronic acid boosters such as Profhilo, and over roughly one to two days for polynucleotides such as Rejuran and Plinest.

bands.title: The following few days
bands.body: Some tenderness and any bruising fade. After a collagen-stimulating booster such as Juvelook, redness and bumps can take a few days to settle.

afterSession.aftercare: Gentle skincare and sun protection, and a short break from heat, strenuous exercise and pressure on the treated area before resuming actives and makeup.

risks.common: Bumps at the injection points, swelling, redness, bruising, tenderness and small palpable lumps, which typically settle over a short period.
risks.lessCommon: Infection, prolonged swelling, nodules and hypersensitivity reactions. Persistent nodules or granuloma formation are a recognised consideration with collagen-stimulating products. Vascular complications are rare but recognised with any facial injection.
cannotDo: It does not add volume or change the shape of the face.
It does not work in a single session. Skin boosters are used as a course, and any change develops gradually.
It is not permanent. Courses are commonly followed by periodic maintenance.
risks.disclose: Tell your doctor about anything in the list under who should postpone or avoid it, and about every previous filler or biostimulator.

costFactors.intro: Kaiteki does not quote prices online, because the product and the amount of it are decided after examining your skin. What moves it:
factors: Which product your doctor selects, and for Juvelook which concentration.
The number and size of areas: a full face, the under-eye area, the neck, hands or décolletage all differ.
The quantity of product your doctor judges appropriate.
How many sessions the course needs, and whether maintenance visits form part of the plan.

comparisons.name: Skin booster
comparisons.bestFor: Skin quality, hydration and fine lines linked to dryness

comparisons.name: Dermal fillers
comparisons.bestFor: Lines and hollows caused by lost volume or structure

comparisons.name: HIFU / Ultherapy
comparisons.bestFor: Laxity and firmness rather than skin quality

relatedReasons.microneedling: Radiofrequency microneedling, considered for texture, acne-scarring and pore concerns where a device rather than an injectable is the route.
relatedReasons.bio-stimulator: Injectables intended to support the skin's own structural renewal, planned across months, where the concern is structure rather than hydration.
relatedReasons.botulinum-toxin: Used for lines caused by muscle movement, which a skin booster does not treat.

sections.heading: What is a skin booster?
body: A skin booster is an injectable treatment that places hydrating and skin-conditioning ingredients into the skin to support its overall quality. Because it is an injectable, it is performed by a doctor.

sections.heading: How is a skin booster different from a filler?
body: A filler is placed to add volume or change contour: a fuller cheek, a defined chin, a corrected hollow. A skin booster is not. It is delivered as small amounts through a series of fine micro-injections spread across the treatment area, and the ingredients are intended to work within the skin itself to support hydration and skin quality over time.

faqs.q: Are skin boosters suitable for sensitive or acne-prone skin?
faqs.a: They may be, once any active acne flare has settled.
Small bumps at each injection point are expected and settle within hours to about a day for hyaluronic acid boosters, and over one to two days for polynucleotides.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: Usually a short course spaced some weeks apart, then periodic maintenance.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Rejuran and Profhilo?
faqs.a: They are built on different ingredients: Rejuran is a salmon-derived polynucleotide, Profhilo a high-concentration hyaluronic acid.

faqs.q: Can I have a skin booster if I am allergic to fish?
faqs.a: Tell your doctor first. Rejuran and Plinest are fish-derived polynucleotides. The hyaluronic acid boosters, such as Profhilo and Hydrodeluxe, are built on a different ingredient.
